evals.prompt: I have a Telegram bot called @storehelper_bot. I need to test its full onboarding flow — when a user sends /start, it should show a language picker with inline buttons, then ask for their name. Can you set up the test environment and walk through the flow?
evals.expected_output: Should ask for session_string first, then resolve the bot, set up a test group, and walk through: /start → capture language buttons → click one → capture name prompt. Should test in both DM and group contexts.
expectations: Asks for session_string before any other action
Resolves the bot username via contacts.resolveUsername
Sets up a test group/supergroup for group-mode testing
Sends /start to the bot in DM context
Identifies inline buttons in the bot's response
Clicks a language button via messages.getBotCallbackAnswer
Verifies the bot asks for a name after language selection
Tests the same flow in group context with addressed command
Provides a summary report with pass/fail for each step

evals.prompt: My bot @quizmaster_bot has a /quiz command that sends multiple-choice questions. Each question has 4 answer buttons. When you click wrong answer it should say 'Try again!' and keep the same question. Right answer should advance to next question. There are 5 questions total. Test the full quiz flow and tell me if anything breaks.
evals.expected_output: Should test the complete quiz flow: trigger /quiz, capture question+buttons, deliberately click wrong answers, verify retry behavior, then click correct answers through all 5 questions. Should also test edge cases like rapid clicking.
expectations: Asks for session_string first
Sends /quiz command to the bot
Captures the first question and its 4 answer buttons
Deliberately clicks a wrong answer and verifies 'Try again!' response
Clicks the correct answer and verifies next question appears
Completes all 5 questions in sequence
Tests rapid button clicking as an edge case
Reports which questions/answers worked and any failures

evals.prompt: I just deployed my bot @referral_bot and it uses deep links for referral tracking. Users open t.me/referral_bot?start=CODE where CODE is a referral code. The bot should greet them with the referrer's name and track the click. I also need you to set up a test group and verify the bot works there too — it should show referral stats when you type /stats in the group.
evals.expected_output: Should test deep links with various referral codes, verify greeting message contains referrer info, set up a test group, add the bot, test /stats command in group context, and report on both DM and group behavior.
expectations: Asks for session_string first
Tests deep link with /start CODE in DM
Tests with valid referral code
Tests with invalid/empty referral code as edge case
Creates or finds a test supergroup
Adds the bot to the group
Promotes the bot to admin (or asks user if it fails)
Tests /stats command in the group
Compares DM vs group behavior in the report
